articleTitle: Object oriented rule-based control on a personal computer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: A rule based control system, known as 'RUBIC' (rule-based intelligent control), has been implemented in SmallTalk to run on a personal computer. RUBIC uses fuzzy logic to decipher the vaguely defined terms such as 'high, low, OK', etc which are used in the control rules, e.g. IF (Temp is LOW) THEN (make a MEDIUM increase to fuel rate). A graphical interface tool, which is linked to every instance of a rule-based object, has been developed to make the system easy to use. The graphics make extensive use of the SmallTalk graphics primitives. The graphics tool is used for entering the control-rules and the fuzzy sets associated with ill-defined quantities such as LOW, HIGH, etc. RUBIC has been used to control temperature in a model of an exothermic reactor and level in a model of a spherical vessel. It is planned to use RUBIC for temperature control on an exothermic pilot plant reactor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Controlling combustion in a double burner boiler using a Prolog rule-base on a personal computer system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: Rules for adjusting, individually, the air-intake to each of a number of burners, depending the concentration of oxygen and of carbon monoxide monitored in their common flue were elicited from energy engineers. The rules, together with a shell and all necessary interfacing software, were coded into Turbo Prolog on a personal computer. An air-inlet valve was fixed to each of 8 burners on one zone of the furnace of a continuous annealing line for rolled steel and a thermocouple and an oxygen and a carbon monoxide analyser set in the common flue. These were connected to the computer via an analog/digital converter and the system was then run successfully with good results on the furnace for about one month until the experimental hardware became unusable. One of five double burner boilers in the steam generating plant of a tinplate finishing works was chosen for long term testing of the system and equipped with durable air-inlet louvres to the burners and an oxygen and a carbon monoxide analyser and a thermocouple in the common flue.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed fermenter control with supervision and data collection by a personal computer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: APV Chemical Machinery and ICI Pharmaceutical Division have jointly developed a laboratory fermenter package and its associated control system. The product, which will be marketed by APV Chemical Machinery, consists of a personal computer linked by a high speed serial bus to two local controllers. Each controller manages a fermenter. The paper outlines the development of the control system part of the package.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wood fibre grading using a low-cost computer vision system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: There is a market for high quality, high strength mouldable hardboard. The quality of hardboard fundamentally depends upon the wood chip stock being given the optimum amount of defibration. Continuous optimal defibration can only be achieved with plant automation. The difficulty is that no effective means of automatically measuring wood defibration exists. The paper describes an initial study of the application of a low-cost computer vision (CV) system to the wood defibration problem. The purpose of the system is to grade the quality of the wood pulp.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Personal computer based statistical process control (PC-SPC) in a manufacturing environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: Statistical process control (SPC) is the application of statistics to the monitoring and control of industrial processes. The paper considers the application of SPC techniques using a personal computer for data capture, processing and storage. It is the result of a study into the possible application of SPC to the manufacture of lamp caps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer control and data processing a four regenerator heat exchanger network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: The equipment consists of two independent pairs of regenerators, which are operated in counter-flow, continuous heat exchange mode. The cold inlet air for each pair comes from a temperature stabilized course at 20 degrees C and enters the regenerator (to be cooled) at the top. After leaving the regenerator, the now warm air is passed through a steam heat exchanger in series with a (1.6 kW) electrical heater which enables accurate control of the hot air inlet temperature to around 120 degrees C. Upon leaving the heater, the now hot air enters the second regenerator at the bottom, flows up the bed, heating the packing in the process, finally being exhausted into the atmosphere via a cooling jacket and rotameters. The four bed regenerators have been interfaced to an Apricot PCXI to provide a system, based on real time control and on line data processing, via a multi-function interface unit (MFIU) and a rig interface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring and control of a turbocharged marine diesel engine using small laboratory microcomputer systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: The work described falls naturally into two separate but related parts. In the first part, three digital control algorithms are examined based on (i) PID (ii) modified deadbeat and (iii) a linguistic rule-based approach and their performance in regulating a medium-sized marine diesel engine is assessed. The other aspect of the work describes a first attempt at providing a graphical interface with the operator for the real-time monitoring of engine parameters. The software is created in the form of a monitoring toolbox and illustrates the concepts which could form the basis of any future on-line diesel engine health monitoring facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent monitoring and control system for a hardboard mill
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: Describes the processes involved in building a plantwide expert process and fiscal control system to: keep the product in trim and maximise profit. The aim was to keep all the board qualities in trim at all times regardless of the varying wood feedstock quality. A PC based local area network (LAN) was installed to monitor and record the entire process. Fifty eight plant variables, moving mimic diagrams and history graphs were displayed at various operator terminals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A distributed monitoring and control system for a sewerage treatment works
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Use of Personal Computer Systems for Plant Monitoring and Control
abstract: The paper describes a low-cost distributed monitoring and control system for a small sewerage treatment works (STW) which is part of Thames Water Authority.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
